content.jointProblem: Can Serbian-specific morphological processing combined with script normalization reduce LinguaBot's retrieval misses while supporting new terminology without a full re-index? The first experiment would compare the current Elasticsearch pipeline against normalization, morphology, and combined variants on held-out support queries, explicitly testing within-word script mixing and new vocabulary; reducing the reported 18% miss rate below 5% remains a hypothesis to test.

rationale.text: His research directly addresses the interaction between Serbian morphological reduction and script normalization, including experimental comparisons of processing order.

sources.quote: U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa.
Koristimo tri stemera dostupna za srpski jezik — dva pravilo-zasnovana i jedan statistički — i kombinujemo ih s fonemskim kanonizacionim korakom opisanim u prethodnim radovima.

rationale.text: He has evaluated phoneme-based canonicalization for Serbian retrieval, providing a concrete candidate for cross-script matching rather than relying solely on manually maintained synonyms.

sources.quote: The phoneme-based canonical form reduced the out-of-vocabulary rate from 9.3% to 2.1% compared with a Latin-only baseline
Precision at rank 10 improved by 8 percentage points over both baselines.

rationale.text: His work offers relevant experience in incremental indexing with script normalization, although it does not establish vocabulary updates without re-indexing in LinguaBot's system.

sources.quote: Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja.
Normalizacija pisma i fonemska kanonizacija implementirane su kao paraleln cevovod koji dodaje manje od 15% vremenske cene u odnosu na sistem bez normalizacije.

rationale.text: He has practical experience introducing normalization into existing enterprise search systems through an add-on, relevant to a bounded integration project.

sources.quote: Ovaj rad opisuje iskustva iz tri pilot implementacije interne pretrage zasnovane na open-source pretražnom okviru dopunjenom modulom za normalizaciju pisma
Administrativni troškovi uvođenja bili su niski jer je modul integrisan kao dodatak bez izmene ostatka sistema.

rationale.text: His production-load research supports evaluating retrieval quality alongside tail latency and comparing deterministic processing with selective neural fallback.

sources.quote: We measure mean reciprocal rank, P@5, and end-to-end latency at the 50th, 90th, and 99th percentiles on a server cluster of four nodes.
A cascaded configuration — deterministic normalizer with neural fallback triggered only for out-of-vocabulary tokens — reaches MRR of 0.66

constraints.text: The solution must address both Serbian inflection and mixed scripts, including within-word typos; improving script conversion alone would leave part of the stated problem unresolved.

sources.quote: Our search misses answers because Serbian words change form (e.g. 'kartica', 'karticu', 'karticom') and users mix Latin and Cyrillic.
our users freely switch between Latin and Cyrillic script mid-sentence — sometimes mid-word in typos.

constraints.text: Integration must accommodate the existing Elasticsearch setup and provide a manageable terminology-update process without a full re-index.

sources.quote: Our current Elasticsearch setup uses a basic stemmer that was built for Croatian and misses a significant share of Serbian-specific forms.
can be updated when new vocabulary arrives without a full re-index.
maintaining those lists manually does not scale as clients add new product terminology every quarter.

constraints.text: Evaluation should use the company's labelled query-response data with linguist validation and distinguish the one-bank baseline sample from performance across all clients.

sources.quote: in a sample of 12,000 real support queries from one bank client, about 18% returned no useful result
We have a labelled query-response dataset of around 85,000 pairs across all clients, and our two in-house linguists can annotate or validate proposed solutions.

constraints.text: The prototype must be testable within six months, with tooling and data work scoped to approximately EUR 8,000; the total research and integration budget still needs clarification.

sources.quote: Budget for tooling or data work is modest — around 8,000 EUR — and we want something testable within six months.

constraints.text: The researcher's contribution must remain a small industrial engagement with a genuine research component, given two active projects; start date and committed effort are unknown.

sources.quote: Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.
nije zainteresovan za opšte projekte razvoja softvera bez istraživačke komponente.

risks: Transfer to short bank and telecom support queries is unvalidated: much of the evidence concerns legal, news, web, or encyclopedia retrieval. The first experiment must stratify real support queries by inflection, cross-script mismatch, within-word mixing, and unfamiliar product terms.

Published incremental insertion of normalized documents does not demonstrate that changing morphology or vocabulary rules preserves compatibility with already indexed terms. A first-stage vocabulary-update experiment must test old and new queries against an unchanged index.

Foreign names, abbreviations, and alphanumeric strings are documented transliteration exceptions. Aggressive normalization or morphological reduction could merge distinct product terms and improve recall while harming precision.
Earlier enterprise pilots still required terminology-related module updates; the evidence does not establish the low-maintenance process LinguaBot needs.
The below-5% miss-rate target is unvalidated, and morphology or script processing alone may not resolve misses caused by missing knowledge-base content or other retrieval failures.

Researcher availability and start date, permitted access to client data, production hardware and latency limits, and funding beyond tooling/data work remain unknown. These could prevent delivery within six months.
questions: Can the researcher confirm a start date and committed effort for a small six-month joint project, and who will own implementation within LinguaBot's engineering team?
What permissions, anonymization, storage, and external-service restrictions apply to sharing bank and telecom queries, labels, and knowledge-base content with the university?
How is 'no useful result' defined, at what retrieval depth, and can linguists establish held-out relevance judgments that separate retrieval errors from missing answers?
Which Elasticsearch version, analyzers, index mappings, and spaCy components are deployed, and what changes are permitted without a full re-index?
What hardware, peak query load, tail-latency limits, and precision-regression limits must the prototype satisfy?
Does the EUR 8,000 cover only tooling and data work, or also researcher fees, integration, compute, and deployment? How much engineering and linguist time is committed?
Which upcoming product terms and within-word mixed-script examples can be reserved for the first update and robustness experiments, and who will maintain normalization rules after the project?
